reason: Conversation 2 correctly identified restricted ventilation from the new drawer as the probable cause, respected the homeowner's refusal to look underneath, and escalated appropriately by telling them to call the fitter back and contact Samsung, while also suggesting filming the fleeting code and keeping a hob-fault/warranty alternative open. Conversation 1 reached the same broad diagnosis but kept pressing the user to look under the hob after they refused, offered a 'test' that could not actually distinguish blocked vents from a failed fan, slapped on an unsupported 'pan misuse' heading despite confirmed induction pans, and never suggested getting the installer back - plus it injected an irrelevant 'suitable replacement' part-lookup panel when no part was justified. Conversation 2's one weakness is slight overconfidence ('pretty much nails it') on what is genuinely uncertain, but it still hedged with a hob-fault pathway, so it served the homeowner clearly better.
